blocks.text: MIN:100–122 DETAILED REVIEW AND DELEGATED APPROVAL — CANONICAL

The packet replaced the incoherent Phase 2 mixture with a first-principles semantic architecture. It compared five candidates per address, scored 45 candidates across 360 criterion values, audited eleven competing families, and ran 51 English Mind concept tests. The pre-approval gate passed 24 checks and all 2,592 deterministic generation assertions. A separate post-migration validation passed 18 checks.

Canonical architecture: the Mind process layer names cognitive representational revision. The second trit selects self-model, target model, or shared cognitive schema; the third selects completed, active, or nonactualized revision.
MIN:100 — completed self-model revision — A completed cognitive process whose result is a change to the cognizer’s representation of the cognizer’s own identity or condition.
MIN:101 — active self-model revision — An active cognitive process that is changing the cognizer’s representation of the cognizer’s own identity or condition.

MIN:102 — nonactualized self-model revision — A cognitive process that would change the cognizer’s representation of the cognizer’s own identity or condition if actualized, but is not active or completed.
MIN:110 — completed target-model revision — A completed cognitive process whose result is a change to a cognizer’s representation of a distinct target.
MIN:111 — active target-model revision — An active cognitive process that is changing a cognizer’s representation of a distinct target.
MIN:112 — nonactualized target-model revision — A cognitive process that would change a cognizer’s representation of a distinct target if actualized, but is not active or completed.
MIN:120 — completed shared-schema revision — A completed cognitive process distributed across multiple cognizers whose result is a change to a representation held in common among them.
MIN:121 — active shared-schema revision — An active cognitive process distributed across multiple cognizers that is changing a representation held in common among them.

MIN:122 — nonactualized shared-schema revision — A cognitive process distributed across multiple cognizers that would change a representation held in common among them if actualized, but is not active or completed.

Design boundary: MIN:1xx owns only change to cognitive representation. It does not make attention, recall, inference, learning as a whole, decision, communication, truth, correction, planning, scheduling, queuing, physical change, or data storage part of the atom. Lexical MIN:*2 means nonactualized revision; it does not mean planned or scheduled.
